introduction_markdown:
Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board, Ordinary Level Examination, June 2020. Chemistry, Paper 2 (subject code 0515). Duration: two and a half hours.

This paper is arranged in three sections, A, B and C. Section A: attempt ALL 5 questions; you will be graded for the best 4 questions answered. Section B: answer BOTH questions in this section. Section C: answer 2 questions out of 3.

In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Non-programmable calculators are allowed. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

**Useful data:** relative atomic masses H = 1.0, C = 12.0, O = 16.0, Cu = 64.0; 1 faraday = 96000 coulombs; molar volume of a gas at r.t.p. = 24000 cm$^3$; specific heat capacity of water = 4.2 J g$^{-1}$ $^\circ$C$^{-1}$; Avogadro number = $6.02\times10^{23}$; $0^\circ$C = 273 K.
enonce_intro_markdown: The elements sodium (Na), Lithium (Li), Potassium (K) and Caesium (Cs) are found in Group I of the Periodic Table.
incertitudes: Points : le sujet imprime (1 mark) apres a(i), (1 mk) manuscrit apres b(i), (2 marks) apres b(ii), (1 mark) apres c(i), (2 marks) apres d (avec un (1mk) manuscrit sur la ligne Use) et (2 marks) apres e ; rien n'est imprime pour a(ii) et c(ii). Recopie des seuls points imprimes par bloc : 1 + 2 + 1 + 2 + 2 = 8, pour « Total = 10 marks ». Le total est recopie tel quel.

Question 2(e)(ii) : le sujet demande une equation equilibree, mais le carbonate de sodium ne se decompose pas a la chaleur d'un bec Bunsen ; le corrige repond « no reaction » avec cette justification (reponse attendue la plus probable).
Question 2(d) : plusieurs usages a grande echelle sont acceptables ; le corrige en donne trois possibles.

Regle de choix de la Section A : l'en-tete dit « ATTEMPT ALL 5 questions. You will be graded for the best 4 », le titre de la section dit « Answer ALL questions ». Les deux sont compatibles ; la regle est codee « 4 sur 5 » (les 4 meilleures comptent), tous les exercices restant a traiter.
Le filigrane (gcerevision.com) et des annotations manuscrites parasites sont ignores ; les pages portent aussi des traces de transparence (texte inverse du verso), sans effet sur la lecture.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) State the common name given to this group of elements. *[1 mark]*

(ii) Why are the elements placed in the same group?
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) The **alkali metals**.

(ii) Because their atoms all have **one electron in the outer shell**, so they have similar chemical properties (each forms a $+1$ ion).

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) How are they stored in the Laboratory?

(ii) Explain. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) They are stored **under oil** (paraffin or kerosene).

(ii) They are very reactive: they react quickly with oxygen and with moisture (water vapour) in the air. The oil keeps air and water away from the metal, so it does not tarnish or react.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Arrange the elements in order of reactivity starting with the least reactive. *[1 mark]*

(ii) State one similarity in the reactivity of Sodium and Potassium with water.
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Li, Na, K, Cs** (least to most reactive). Reactivity increases down the group because the outer electron is further from the nucleus and is lost more easily.

(ii) Both react with cold water to give **hydrogen gas and an alkaline solution of the hydroxide** (they float, fizz and move about on the surface). For example $2\mathrm{Na} + 2\mathrm{H_2O} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{NaOH} + \mathrm{H_2}$ and $2\mathrm{K} + 2\mathrm{H_2O} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{KOH} + \mathrm{H_2}$.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) How is sodium extracted? State one large scale use of sodium metal.

Method of extraction: ...

Use: ... *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Method of extraction:** electrolysis of **molten sodium chloride** (in the Downs cell). At the cathode $\mathrm{Na^+} + e^- \rightarrow \mathrm{Na}$; at the anode chlorine gas is given off.

**Use (one is enough):** a coolant (heat exchanger) in nuclear reactors; or manufacture of other sodium compounds such as sodium peroxide and sodium cyanide; or sodium vapour street lamps.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Write balanced equations to show the effect of heat on the following substances.

(i) $\mathrm{KNO_3}$

(ii) $\mathrm{Na_2CO_3}$ *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) Potassium nitrate decomposes to the nitrite and oxygen:

$2\mathrm{KNO_3} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{KNO_2} + \mathrm{O_2}$

(Balance check: K 2 = 2, N 2 = 2, O 6 = 4 + 2.)

(ii) Sodium carbonate is **not decomposed** by heating at laboratory (Bunsen) temperatures: **no reaction**. (Of the Group I carbonates only lithium carbonate decomposes: $\mathrm{Li_2CO_3} \rightarrow \mathrm{Li_2O} + \mathrm{CO_2}$.)
